deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a category C with a class W of weak equivalences and a class Cof of cofibrations, with an initial object ∅. This is a Brown/Waldhausen-style 'cofibration category', i.e. half of a Quillen model structure. Grothendieck has built an auxiliary category C̃ with the same objects as C. A morphism x→y in C̃ is a class of pairs (f,i): f: x→ȳ in C and i: y→ȳ in W∩Cof, taken up to a relation ~. Such a pair is meant to stand for the right fraction [i]^{-1}[f]. The aim is to compare C̃ with the localization W^{-1}C, i.e. to describe the homotopy category by fractions with trivial-cofibration denominators.

Step 1 (the 'weak lifting lemma', which is in substance K.S. Brown's factorization lemma, dualized). Let f: x→y be in W with y cofibrant. The NB stresses that cofibrancy of y is the only hypothesis used. Then f factors as f = αi with:
- i: x→x̄ in W∩Cof;
- α: x̄→y in W;
- α having a section g: y→x̄, αg = 1_y.
The standard proof factors (f,1): x⊔y→y as a cofibration followed by a weak equivalence. Then x→x⊔y is a cofibration because it is the pushout of ∅→y; this is why only y∈Cof is needed. Finally i∈W by 2-out-of-3.

Step 2 (abandoned attempt). Grothendieck wants to show that the C̃-morphism (g,i): y→x is an inverse of f inside C̃. For (gf,i) ~ 1_x he would use the evident commutative diagram. This fails because the relation ~ seems to require a cofibration, and αi = f lies in W but not necessarily in Cof. It would work if one could post-compose with some β: y→y' making βf a cofibration. He notes this is false in general: take Cof = monomorphisms and f not mono. Verdict: 'Ça se présente mal !'

Step 3 (change of strategy). Instead he defines the canonical functor C̃ → W^{-1}C, sending x to x and (f,i) to [i]^{-1}[f]. It respects identities and composition, and it is bijective on objects (he corrects 'surjectif' to 'bijectif').
- Claim: it is full ('surjectif sur les flèches').
- Every morphism of W^{-1}C is a composite of maps [h] and inverses [f]^{-1} with f∈W. So it suffices to show each [f]^{-1} comes from C̃.
- The image of (g,i) is [i]^{-1}[g]. From αi = f one gets [f][i]^{-1} = [α], hence [f][i]^{-1}[g] = [α][g] = [αg] = [1_y].
- Since [f] is invertible, [i]^{-1}[g] = [f]^{-1}.

This is one step towards the standard theorem: in a cofibration category, the homotopy category restricted to cofibrant objects is computed by fractions i^{-1}f with i a trivial cofibration (Brown 1973; later Cisinski, Rădulescu-Banu).
errors: Step 2 is a dead end, but Grothendieck recognizes it himself and gives a correct counterexample (Cof = monos, f not mono). There is no actual error.

The fullness argument in Step 3 is correct. It needs y cofibrant, which the NB records. Fullness for morphisms with non-cofibrant target is not addressed on this page; presumably C̃ is restricted to cofibrant objects or this is handled elsewhere.
Faithfulness of C̃ → W^{-1}C, i.e. that ~ is exactly the kernel, is not treated on this page.

ideas.what: Factorization of a weak equivalence f: x→y with y cofibrant as f = αi, with i a trivial cofibration and α a weak equivalence admitting a section g; only cofibrancy of y is needed.
ideas.usually_credited_to: K.S. Brown (1973), Abstract homotopy theory and generalized sheaf cohomology
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in Pursuing Stacks (1983) discussions of model categories; not specifically known

ideas.what: Category C̃ of right fractions (f,i) with i ∈ W∩Cof, and the canonical functor C̃ → W^{-1}C, bijective on objects and shown to be full.
ideas.modern_name: Calculus of fractions / homotopy category of a cofibration category via trivial-cofibration denominators

ideas.what: Observation that a weak equivalence cannot in general be made a cofibration by post-composition (counterexample: Cof = monos, f not mono).
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction to the naive inverse in the fraction category

missed.claim: Historical: by August 1982, before Pursuing Stacks, Grothendieck's stack notes already work through Brown-type cofibration-category axiomatics and the description of W^{-1}C by fractions. This documents his engagement with abstract homotopy theory earlier than usually emphasized. The mathematics itself is standard.
missed.quote: On va donc plutôt définir d'abord le foncteur canonique C̃ ⟶ W^{-1}C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Dates the pre-history of Pursuing Stacks and its modelizer ideas; of interest to historians, not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification in a cofibration category: Brown's factorization lemma plus fullness of the fraction-category functor. It is correct and well known since Brown 1973. Only mild historical interest from the 1982 date.
transcription_corrections: The marginal NB likely reads 'NB Je n'utilise y ∈ Cof qu'ici' (cofibrancy of y used only here), not 'On utilise y ∈ Cof ici'.
The object-assignment line '$\xi' x \longmapsto x$' is probably 'Ob x ↦ x' or simply 'x ↦ x'; the 'ξ'' is likely a misreading.
'{+cherché [?]+}' under 'l'inverse' plausibly reads 'cherché'; the struck words after it are illegible.
In the second diagram the struck label near 1_x looks like a crossed-out arrow, not '1̄_x'.
Marginal 'g' under the factorization: 'α admet une section g, αg = 1_y' is correct.
